dashboard.title: Best opportunities right now
dashboard.subtitle: Every market on your watchlist has been scanned. Ordered by readiness and setup quality — never by AI confidence.
dashboard.noOpportunities: Nothing qualifies right now. Standing aside is a decision.

quality.label: Setup Quality
quality.notProbability: This is a setup quality grade, not a win probability.

confidence.label: AI confidence
confidence.hint: Separate from Setup Quality. This is how sure the analysis layer is about its own read, based on data quality and timeframe agreement.

plan.label: Entry plans
plan.bestPriceHint: Better fill, higher chance price never reaches it.
plan.saferPriceHint: Worse fill, less guesswork because confirmation is already visible.

explain.factsHint: Every number here was calculated from candles in code, not written by a language model.
explain.interpretationHint: This is a reading of the facts. It can be wrong.
explain.assumptionsHint: What must stay true for the read to hold.
explain.whatIfPlaceholder: e.g. what if price sweeps below the zone and reclaims it quickly?

setups.title: All setups
setups.subtitle: Grouped by scanner state
setups.invalidatedKept: Invalidated setups are kept, never deleted, so you can review what the read got wrong.

signal.title: Signals
signal.subtitle: Only the markets actually calling a trade, with the entry, stop, targets and the reasoning behind them

tierHint.ENTRY_NOW: Conditions are met. Entry is valid now, per the plan.
tierHint.WAIT_CONFIRMATION: Price has reached the zone. The trigger listed on the detail page is still outstanding.
tierHint.LIMIT_ZONE: Price has not reached the zone yet. A resting order at the zone is the play.

none.title: No signal right now
none.body: Nothing is broken — this is the system working. A market whose conditions are not met is held back rather than promoted into a signal. On a session where the timeframes disagree across the board, no signal is the correct answer.
none.blockedTitle: What each market is stuck on

replay.title: Market replay training
replay.subtitle: Reveal the chart one candle at a time, decide before you can see the future, then check the result.
replay.end: End of the data set. Restart to practise again.
replay.noFuture: Every timeframe is truncated to the replay clock, so the engine only reads candles that have already closed. No future data leaks in.
replay.engineRead: What the engine reads right now
replay.yourCall: What do you think happens next?
replay.callHint: Choose before revealing the next candle. The result is checked against what actually happened over the following 10 candles.
replay.waitingResult: Call recorded. Reveal 10 more candles to see the result.
replay.resultFlat: Price barely moved, scored as a draw.
replay.practiceHint: The goal is not a high hit rate. It is making your reasoning at decision time match what the chart was actually showing.

log.title: Every practice trade
log.subtitle: Each call you made, with the entry price, the exit price and the real result.
log.empty: No calls yet. Make one to start the log.
log.windowClose: Measurement window closed, exited at market
log.ambiguous: One candle touched both the stop and the target. Candle data does not say which came first, so this is scored as a stop — the outcome against us. We do not guess in our own favour.
log.noEnginePlan: The engine had no plan at that moment, so a 1.5xATR stop and a 2R target were used to make the call measurable.
log.engineAtCall: What the engine saw when you called it
log.stayedOutGood: Standing aside was right: price barely moved.
log.stayedOutMissed: Price did travel, so this one was missed (which is still fine if your reasoning was sound).
log.reviewHint: Review what you were thinking and what the chart then did. That is the part that builds skill — not the hit rate.

summary.title: This session
summary.notEnough: Too few trades for these numbers to say anything about skill. The per-trade reasoning is the useful part.

replay.callRecorded: Call recorded. Keep stepping the chart; it settles when the stop or the target is reached.
